title: Attention-dispatch tuner: bucketized micro-bench + online rehearse for kernel selection
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: reduce average token latency and p99 for attention-heavy workloads by selecting the most efficient attention kernel variant per-architecture and per-sequence-length bucket at runtime. Approach: combine an offline micro-benchmark sweep (matrix of [arch x batch x seqlen x model-dtype] -> cost/latency profiles) with a lightweight online rehearser that validates candidate kernel choices on a small sampled traffic, and an exploration policy (epsilon-decay bandit with cost penalty) to adapt to shifting request distributions. We will integrate with existing prefill/decode scheduler so that the dispatch decision can differ for prefill vs decode phases, and use cached prefix fingerprints to pick cached-friendly kernels. Implementation: (1) profiler job that produces bucket profiles and stores into a small key-value store keyed by (arch, seqlen_bucket, dtype, model_family); (2) runtime adapter that consults the profile and applies a bandit score adjusted by recent rehearse trials; (3) rehearse path that samples <0.5% of requests to run alternative kernel in shadow/opt-in mode and report metrics; (4) rollout knobs and safe-fallbacks to a conservative kernel if latency/regressions exceed thresholds. This ticket covers the adapter + rehearse integration, experiments, and rollout plan. We will not change kernel implementations themselves in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter consults offline profiles and picks a kernel variant within the first dispatch decision for >99% of requests
Rehearse flow runs shadowed alternative kernel on sampled traffic and reports per-kernel delta metrics to the dashboard
End-to-end canary shows >=8% average token-cost reduction for GPT-style attention at seq-len buckets [64, 128, 256] on T4 and A100 compared to baseline kernel selector
Graceful fallback triggers if p95 latency increases >10% within a 10-minute window during canary
Integration tests simulate prefill->decode transition and verify kernel switch does not corrupt KV cache usage or decoding outputs
notes: We prefer bucketization over per-seqlen exact mapping to keep profile store small and robust to jitter
Tradeoff: more aggressive exploration yields faster adaptation but increases short-term variance; default epsilon=0.05 for first 48h of rollout
We will eventually fold quantization profiles (int8/int4) into same keyspace; this ticket scaffolds the key layout
Telemetry: token-level latency, kernel-execution time, OOM/Retry counts, and cost-estimate per-token must be emitted for each rehearse sample
comments: 2026-01-21 — Asha Patel: Created ticket after spike showed large variance in kernel choice across seq-lens. Initial microbench shows A100 benefits from tiled attention for seqlen <= 128 but regresses at longer lengths for some model dims.

2026-02-02 — Diego Morales: Ran extended microbench across T4, A100, and H100 emulators. Added seqlen buckets: [1-32], [33-64], [65-128], [129-256], [257+]. Observed p50 latency improvements up to 22% on tiled kernels in middle buckets.
2026-02-18 — ML Infra review (Sophie Lin): Agreed on rehearse sample size <=0.5% and shadow-run policy; asked to ensure rehearse path does not consume extra KV cache entries across warm-starts.

2026-02-28 — Diego Morales: Implemented profile store schema and adapter prototype. Running canary on internal workload with 5k qps; initial results show 6% cost reduction but occasional 12% p95 spikes at high-burst; hunting down scheduling contention with prefill threads.

2026-03-10 — Diego Morales: Mitigated p95 spikes by delaying non-essential rehearse trials during high CPU contention windows and by giving prefill dispatch a higher priority lane. New canary run shows p95 stable and average token-cost reduction 9%.

2026-03-12 — Asha Patel: Ready for broader staging rollout pending one integration test fix for decode-phase kernel switch (see test #42). Next steps: finalize rollout ramp plan and add opt-out flag per-customer.
